title: Solitude on the Turquoise Waters of the Canadian Rockies
excerpt: Glacial rock flour creates unreal hues of electric blue in Banff and Jasper. An autumn field expedition paddling across morning mist.
content:
At 6:00 AM, Moraine Lake is completely still. The ten peaks of the Wenkchemna Range stand mirrored with flawless clarity in water so startlingly turquoise it looks painted. This distinctive luminescence is caused by glacial silt suspended in water melting directly from high icefields.

Paddling our cedar-strip canoe toward the western bay, the only sound was the rhythmic dip of the ash paddle and the far-off murmur of a cascading waterfall. Autumn had turned the larch trees on the higher slopes to brilliant gold, creating a breathtaking contrast against the first dusting of winter snow.
author: Maya Lin
